claims.text: The initial material can be an additively manufactured, initially coarse-grained, single-phase CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
The as-manufactured coarse-grained HEA has high ductility and non-brittle, dislocation-dominated behavior under moderate sliding.
UHV excludes chemically reactive environmental species and suppresses oxidation-related surface films during sliding.
Performing the tests in UHV prevents impurity segregation.
Highly localized sliding shear produces severe plastic deformation and dynamically refines the initially coarse surface microstructure.
Sliding refinement produces a nanocrystalline surface layer with a critical grain size of approximately 10–50 nm.
At the critical grain size, deformation changes from dislocation slip to grain-boundary-dominated processes such as grain-boundary sliding.
Nanocrystalline CoCrFeMnNi can become susceptible to grain-boundary decohesion or cavitation even without significant segregation or phase separation.
The grain-boundary-dominated deformation and decohesion produce brittle behavior and an abrupt loss of ductility.
The brittle transition will be accompanied by increased friction or altered wear patterns.
The transition will produce brittle fracture features, including cavitation along grain boundaries.
Temperature and shear rate influence grain-size-dependent surface shear strength and friction.
Intermediate temperatures and high strain rates can induce refinement while avoiding thermally activated phase separation.
Conventional alloys require impurity segregation or brittle grain-boundary precipitation to display the corresponding brittle response.
At very high temperatures, thermal segregation or related processes may override the sliding-induced refinement mechanism.
At very low strain rates, dynamic grain refinement may be insufficiently activated.
A controlled comparison should expose the HEA and a conventional impurity-embrittled alloy to identical UHV sliding tests while varying temperature and strain rate.
Grain size, mechanical response, friction, wear rate, and fracture morphology should be measured and correlated during the comparison.
Failure to observe a grain-size-correlated ductile-to-brittle transition in the HEA under high-strain UHV sliding would falsify the hypothesis.
The exact critical grain size, the relative roles of grain-boundary sliding, decohesion, and cavitation, and the possible contribution of subtle segregation remain unresolved.
